$schema_note: Reflex table v1, 2026-09-17. Codes verified by compiling with rustc 1.93.0 and GHC 9.12.2 unless verified=false. next_step vocabulary: cargo_fix (apply machine-applicable suggestions: `cargo fix --allow-dirty` or `cargo clippy --fix --allow-dirty`, then re-run; if the diagnostic persists, fall through to llm_patch), run_fmt (`cargo fmt`), add_import (the diagnostic names the path; add the use/import line), rerun (same command once), llm_patch (a model reads the code and edits), escalate (a person or reasoning model decides). Precedence: (1) rustfmt diff -> run_fmt; (2) an error code or lint name in the FIRST error -> this table; (3) test-runner output -> test classes; (4) no code -> Jev over the code-less class list.

E0369.note: binary op on a type without the impl

E0596.note: rustc suggests `mut`; machine-applicable, so try cargo_fix first

E0425.note: add_import only when the diagnostic carries `help: consider importing`; otherwise llm_patch

E0432.note: the import line itself is wrong; a typo or a missing dependency

E0599.note: add_import only when the output says `items from traits can only be used if the trait is in scope`; otherwise llm_patch

E0117.note: a design constraint, not a local edit

$syntax.note: rustc parse errors carry NO E-code: `error: expected `;`, found keyword `let``. Match `error: expected` / `error: unexpected` before falling through to Jev.

rustc_lints.$note: Names as printed after `-D` (hyphenated) or inside `#[warn(...)]` (underscored); normalize to one form. Under `-D warnings` these print as `error:` with no E-code.

unused-variables.note: the underscore suggestion is MaybeIncorrect; deleting may hide a bug

dead-code.note: deleting a function is a judgment

clippy.$rule: Any `clippy::<lint>` name: next_step = cargo_fix (`cargo clippy --fix --allow-dirty`), rebuild, repeat up to 3 times because a fix can surface new lints; if a lint persists, llm_patch. No allowlist: only MachineApplicable suggestions are applied, so the fix tool is the allowlist. class = clippy_lint.

ghc.$note: Codes print as [GHC-NNNNN]. GHC-18042 is the -Werror wrapper and carries no class; take the other code on the line.

GHC-25897.note: rigid type variable or occurs check

GHC-39999.note: no instance, ambiguous type variable, or a function applied to too few args surfacing as Show (a -> b)

GHC-88464.note: variable not in scope; add_import only if the name is qualified or the message says `Perhaps you want to add ... to the import list`

GHC-76037.note: qualified name (`Set.fromList`) or type constructor: add_import; an unqualified record field name here is a code error: llm_patch

GHC-87110.note: cabal dependency or exposed-modules change; a build-file edit

GHC-66111.note: unused import under -Werror; GHC prints the exact import to remove, a mechanical edit but no fix tool applies it

GHC-38417.note: GHC prints the inferred signature; mechanical but no fix tool

test_runner.$note: nextest and libtest output has no codes. Match these literal markers in order; the first match wins.

panicked at.note: unwrap on None, index out of bounds, unreachable, explicit panic, or assert!(cond, msg) which prints only msg

environment.$note: Match anywhere in the output; these precede the code table because they explain the codes that follow them.

jev_codeless_classes.$note: MECE class list for output with no code, no lint name, no test marker and no environment marker. Names are what the output literally shows. This is the Choice criteria map; keep it under 12 entries.
jev_codeless_classes.syntax_error: The compiler could not parse the source: `expected ... found ...`, `unexpected token`, `parse error on input`.
jev_codeless_classes.type_mismatch: The compiler accepted the syntax but a value's type does not match what its position requires, including wrong argument counts and missing or unknown fields.
jev_codeless_classes.name_resolution: A name, module, type, trait, or method could not be found in scope.
jev_codeless_classes.ownership_or_lifetime: A borrow, move, mutability, or lifetime rule was violated.
jev_codeless_classes.instance_or_trait: A required instance or trait implementation is missing, ambiguous, or overlapping.
jev_codeless_classes.unused_or_style_lint: A warning promoted to error about an unused item, naming, or style; the code would otherwise compile.
jev_codeless_classes.test_failure: The program compiled and a test reported a failure, panic, or assertion.
jev_codeless_classes.test_hang_or_crash: A test timed out or the process died from a signal.
jev_codeless_classes.build_environment: Tooling, network, disk, locks, build scripts, linking, or dependency resolution failed; not a source-code error.
jev_codeless_classes.multiple_unrelated: Several errors of different kinds whose first one is not clearly the cause.

jev_codeless_next_step.cargo_fix: run `cargo fix --allow-dirty` or `cargo clippy --fix --allow-dirty` and rebuild; the diagnostic offers a machine-applicable suggestion
jev_codeless_next_step.add_import: add the `use` or `import` line the diagnostic names and rebuild
jev_codeless_next_step.rerun: rerun the same command once; only for locks, timeouts, network, or a build script that failed on I/O
jev_codeless_next_step.llm_patch: a model must read the code and write a fix, including any deterministic panic or assertion in code under test
jev_codeless_next_step.escalate: a person or reasoning model must decide; the fix changes a design, a dependency, or the environment
